newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: ADB says lending barely grew in 1996.
newsitem.headline: ADB says lending barely grew in 1996.

text.p: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) said on Monday its total volume of lending and equity investments in 1996 amounted to $5.65 billion, up only marginally from $5.62 billion in 1995.

Lending through the bank's soft loans window, the Asian Development Fund (ADF) which helps the poorest countries in the region, amounted to $1.67 billion, the bank said in its annual report published on Monday. In 1995, the bank gave $1.45 billion in loans through the ADF.
The Manila-based multilateral financial institution, owned by 56 countries, has during its 30 years in existence given cumulative loans amounting to $62.17 billion.
Its ADF funding has played an important role in the development of much needed infrastructure in Asia's most backward regions.
But with the development of financial markets and concepts like build-operate-transfer, private sector flows in the region have outstripped the bank's lending.
Exact figures of private sector flows in the region were not available but analysts say they exceeded the bank's lending.

ADB officials have said the bank is now concentrating on being a catalyst for growth by investing in the first few projects in a region and calling the attention of entrepreneurs to that area's growth prospects.
The bank is due to hold its annual meeting in Fukuoka, Japan, from May 11 to 13 and one of the issues likely to come up is the bank's future role.

Last month, the bank helped finance ministers of the 18-nation Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in discussing a plan that will enable the grouping to fulfill its goal of lifting all trade barriers in the region.
APEC is the world's largest potential trade grouping.
